stories.title: Poland says Starlink station fire 'act of sabotage'
stories.summary: Polish Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said Warsaw believed the attack aimed to disrupt internet access for the Ukrainian military, calling it "an element of the next phase of hybrid warfare."

"This act of sabotage was deliberately designed to disable the station ... disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army," Gawkowski, who also serves as digital minister, told public broadcaster TVP. He said the fire at the station belonging to Polish state-owned telecom company Exatel broke out late on Wednesday. "There is much to suggest that we are dealing with an element of the next phase of hybrid warfare," he said. The deputy premier said that the station was used to transmit internet traffic through Poland, including to neighboring Ukraine . He also said there were "many indications" suggesting the incident "fits into this new Russian doctrine of attack." Its military said the Mi-8 aircraft had crossed from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad on Wednesday morning, penetrating Polish airspace to a depth of about 300 metres (328 yards) and staying for 42 seconds north of Braniewo. stories.article_text_excerpt: Europe faces major challenges to its competitiveness, including low productivity growth, labour shortages, demographic decline and technological gaps. While these issues dominate economic discussions, a significant opportunity often remains overlooked: accessibility. Around 90 million people in the European Union live with disabilities, and this number is expected to increase as the population ages. Yet employment rates among people with disabilities remain far below the EU average, leaving a substantial pool of talent, skills and purchasing power underutilized. By making products, services, buildings and digital platforms accessible, businesses can reach a wider audience, including people with disabilities, older adults, individuals with temporary limitations and consumers who simply benefit from better design.
